previous_body: L118 Eagles and other large birds ride the warm air
that rises along mountain slopes, so they can soar
for hours while they barely move their wings.
L119 Machu Picchu in Peru sits high in the Andes,
and its ruins still show how the Inca built stone
walls and farm terraces on very steep land.
L120 Mountains store fresh water as snow and ice,
and the slow melt each summer feeds rivers that
millions of people use for drinking and farming.

[0m[38;5;15m●[0m L121 K2 on the border of Pakistan and China is the
second highest mountain on Earth, and many climbers
say it is more dangerous than Everest.
L122 On a mountain, the side that faces the sun gets
more warmth and light, so snow melts sooner there
and different plants can grow on each side.
L123 Shepherds in many mountain regions move their
sheep and goats up to high pastures in summer and
bring them back down to the valleys before winter.
L124 Lightning often strikes high peaks and ridges
during summer storms, so hikers should leave exposed
ground early when dark clouds begin to build.
L125 The Ural Mountains in Russia run for more than
two thousand kilometers, and they are often seen as
a border between Europe and Asia.
L126 Mountain lakes often form in hollows that
glaciers carved long ago, and their water can look
deep blue or bright green because of fine rock dust.
L127 Climbers on the highest peaks often carry
bottles of oxygen, because above about eight
thousand meters the air holds very little oxygen.
L128 Some mountain roads climb with many sharp bends
called switchbacks, which let cars and trucks go up
a steep slope at a safer, gentler angle.
L129 Old stories in many cultures say that gods or
spirits live on high mountains, and Mount Olympus
was the home of the gods in ancient Greek myths.
L130 Standing on a mountain top after a long climb,
you can see far across the land below, and many
people say the view makes the hard work worth it.
